correctness.rationale: Every primitive signed excursion of semilength ℓ has C_{ℓ−1} shapes per sign and contributes that semilength in the matching occupation variable and one return, including at the terminal step. Thus with P(z)(1−P(z))=z the marked function is F=1/[1−u(P(x)+P(y))]. At u=1 the Catalan divided difference has coefficient C_n in each occupation. Its u-derivative is F(x,y,1)^2−F(x,y,1), giving the stated conditional mean. Subtracting adjacent coefficient rectangles leaves the positive middle Catalan sum before the center and the zero central tie for odd n; reflection gives the other half. The endpoint is C_{n+1}/C_n−1=3n/(n+2). Stirling asymptotics of the Catalan products uniformly away from the boundary convert √n times the increments to the integral of [v(1−v)]^{−3/2}/√π from t to 1−t. The uniform bound on earlier unscaled increments follows by bounding the half-sum by a constant times Σ_{s≥j+1}s^{−3/2}, so the initial δn increments contribute O(√δ) after scaling. Integrating the resulting increment profile yields (8/√π)√{t(1−t)}, including the center by the same summation. Conditional fair signs give E[A|lengths]=n/2 and E[(A−n/2)²|lengths]=H/4, H=Σℓ_i². Marking one excursion of squared length gives 2D²P/(1−2P)^2; a return mark adds the factor (1+2P)/(1−2P) for KH. Coefficients give E[H]=n(n+2)/3, E[KH]=4^{n−1}n(n+3)/binom(2n,n)−E[H], and E[K]=4^n/binom(2n,n)−1. Subtraction and the factor 1/4 yield the exact negative covariance and its stated limit. At n=1 all means equal one and both covariances vanish; at n=2 the means are (3/2,2,3/2) and quadratic covariance −1/9. Frozen verification notes and verifier were inspected, not executed. Neither the reported enumeration nor a Brownian scaling analogy is used as proof of pointwise conditioning.

value.rationale: Uniform occupation and an unconditional return-count law do not answer how frequent zero returns are among bridges with a specified imbalance. The evaluated shape and conditional scaling distinguish a bounded endpoint mean from a √n interior mean and locate the maximizing occupations exactly. This is usable for comparing occupation-conditioned bridge ensembles; the value does not depend on the separately indexed covariance being new or on asserting any ordering of full conditional distributions.
